issues.failure_explanation: The Gronwall step bounds y_1(T')+∫_0^{T'}y_2 for each T', i.e. sup_{T'}(y_1(T')+∫_0^{T'}y_2). But Υ(T_M)=sup y_1+∫_0^{T_M}y_2, which can be up to twice that. Counterexample: B=0 (or tiny B), a=0, y_2≡A/T, y_1(t)=A(1-t/T). The hypothesis holds with equality and (cond_prop31) holds, yet sup y_1+∫y_2=2A>δAE for every δ<2. The conclusion with δ>1 arbitrary is therefore false. The proof would need 2(A+BTθ^{1+β})E<θ, which is stronger than the stated condition, even for δ=8.

failure_location.quote: This implies $\Upsilon\left(T_M\right)<\theta$, hence $T_M=T$, and thus proves the Lemma if $A>0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the continuation set with sup_{T'}(y_1+∫y_2), or accept a factor 2. The lemma then holds for δ>2 with condition ((δ-2)/(2δBTE))^{1/β}. Restate stab_thm and main_thm i) with this δ range and condition, and redo the numerics and the remark on δ.
issues.overall_effect: The stated conclusion and condition (cond_prop31), and the claimed improvement 'choosing δ=8 ... factor 7^{1/β}', are not established. Theorem stab_thm, its corollary and part i) of main_thm inherit the false estimate with δ close to 1, including δ=3/2 used in the experiments.
issues.title: Adjusted Gronwall lemma: pointwise bound on y_1+∫y_2 does not control sup y_1+∫y_2
issues.why_classification: A contained reformulation (factor 2, restricted δ, modified condition) gives a recognizably comparable result. The qualitative method survives, but constants and the δ regime change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where we used the Sobolev embedding $H^1 \hookrightarrow L^6$ and elliptic regularity in the first step, Hölder's inequality and again the Sobolev embedding $H^1 \hookrightarrow L^6$ in the second step

issues.failure_explanation: Hölder and Sobolev give ||e||_{L^3} ≤ ||e||_{L^2}^{1/2}||e||_{L^6}^{1/2} ≤ C_S^{1/2}||e||_{L^2}^{1/2}||e||_{H^1}^{1/2}, with the full norm (||e||^2+|e|^2)^{1/2}. The text replaces ||e||_{H^1} by the seminorm |e|_{H^1}, which is false: for e≡const≠0 the right side is 0 while ||e||_{L^3}>0. e is not mean-free in general, since ∫ρ̄ need not equal ∫ρ_0. Correcting this adds a term of type |e|_{H^1}||e||_{L^2}^2, which after Young gives a quartic term ||e||^4. This changes the structure of (energy_esti), with exponent β=1 mixed with β=2 and a different B.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the estimate of II with the full H^1 norm. Extend the Gronwall lemma and the continuation argument to a two-term nonlinearity (or absorb the extra term into a(t)). Recompute B and the conditions.
issues.overall_effect: The constant B=108C_S^6C_ell^4 and the single nonlinearity of the form B||e||^4||e||^2 in (energy_esti) are not justified. Conditions (stab_cond) and (root) are therefore unreliable, as are the availability results in the numerics.
issues.title: Seminorm used in place of the H^1 norm in the Sobolev interpolation for the cubic term II
issues.why_classification: The repair is local to the energy estimate plus a modified Gronwall and continuation step. The overall conditional-stability architecture survives with changed constants.

issues.failure_explanation: c̄ satisfies only the scalar condition ∂_n c̄=0. This does not give a boundary condition for each component of ∇c̄, and the vector Laplacian of ∇c̄ has nonzero normal derivative on ∂Ω in general. For example, on (0,1)^2 the normal component of ∇c̄ satisfies a Dirichlet condition and the tangential one a Neumann condition. The weak form of the stated vector problem therefore has an uncontrolled boundary term. The estimator η_∞ has interior jumps only (no boundary or Dirichlet terms), so the Demlow-type max-norm bound is applied to a problem it does not cover. The computable bound ||q_h||_∞+C_∞η_∞ on ||∇c̄||_{L^∞} is therefore unjustified.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose $(\rho,c)$ is a weak solution of the Keller-Segel system (\ref{KS1}), (\ref{KS2}), (\ref{KScond}) and $(\bar{\rho},\bar{c})$ be a solution to (\ref{res_bdrKS}), as above.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem stab_thm and Theorem stab_cont assume that a weak solution exists on the whole of [0,T], which is the very conclusion of the corollaries. Proposition apostverif needs the bound (unif_bound) on [0,min{T,T_max}], including T_max, where ρ may not exist. The missing argument is to apply the stability result on [0,T'] for T'<min{T,T_max}, show that A, E and the conditions are monotone in T', and pass to the limit. The same applies to (root) and partial time intervals. This is not carried out, and main_thm's 'in particular (ρ,c) is a weak solution up to time T' has no proof, since its proof cites only the stability theorems.

failure_location.quote: Suppose further that (\ref{stab_cond}) is satisfied and that $A$ as well as $E$ are finite.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the argument: stability on [0,T'] for all T'<min{T,T_max}, with monotonicity of A, E, (stab_cond) and the roots of (root) in T', a uniform L^2 bound on [0,T_max), then the blow-up criterion. Cite it explicitly in main_thm.
issues.overall_effect: The headline claim that satisfaction of the condition implies existence of a weak solution on [0,T] is supported only by a circular 'direct consequence'.
issues.title: Existence conclusion uses stability theorems that presuppose a weak solution on [0,T]
issues.why_classification: A short monotonicity and limit argument closes the gap without changing any claim or condition.

issues.failure_explanation: (noncomp_esti) bounds ||e(t)||^2+∫_{t^n}^t|e|^2 for each t, i.e. sup_t of the sum. The continuation set I_n and the 'implies' step need sup_s||e(s)||^2+∫_{t^n}^t|e|^2, which can be twice as large (same defect as in the Gronwall lemma). Hence the strict inequality and the contradiction with maximality of t* are not obtained. The passage to the global bound sup_{[0,T]}||e||^2+∫_0^T|e|^2 ≤ Ψ_{N_t-1} is also only sketched. It states ||e(t^{n+1})||^2≤Ψ_n, but the integral over [0,T] is a sum of N_t local integrals and needs a cumulative argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define I_n through sup_s(||e(s)||^2+∫_{t^n}^s|e|^2). Carry the accumulated dissipation through the recursion, as in the cumulative bound G(t)=||e(t)||^2+∫_0^t|e|^2. State the final bound as sup+∫ ≤ 2Ψ_{N_t-1}, or modify δ_n and the root condition accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The local-in-time estimate with δ_n the smallest root of (root), and the global bound Ψ_{N_t-1}, are not established as stated. This affects the 'local conditions' comparison and the existence statement based on ii).
issues.title: Local continuation argument bounds sup+∫ using an estimate for sup of (y_1+∫y_2); global assembly unjustified
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained reworking of the continuation set, the recursion and the final constant. The comparable result survives with a modified root condition.
